strategy_specs.name: Midterm-cycle seasonal + trend
strategy_specs.thesis: Q4 of the midterm year through the pre-election year is historically the strongest cycle window; a 200d trend filter limits damage when a policy or macro shock overrides seasonality.

inputs.units: price adjusted for splits and dividends (total-return close)
inputs.release: available at the 16:00 ET close of the bar date

inputs.units: percent per year, discount basis
inputs.release: Federal Reserve H.15, posted next business day

strategy_specs.signal: sweet = (year mod 4 = 2 and month >= 10) or year mod 4 = 3; up = SPY close > SMA200(SPY close).
strategy_specs.entry: Weight = 100% (sweet and up), 60% (sweet, not up), 70% (not sweet, up), 30% (neither); capped at 98%.
strategy_specs.exit: No separate exit: the weekly target replaces the position; the remainder sits in T-bills.
strategy_specs.decision_time: close of the first bar of each ISO week
strategy_specs.execution: market order at the next bar's open
strategy_specs.invalidation: The seasonal tilt is the hypothesis: if the 2026-27 window underperforms SPY while SPY is above its 200-day average, drop the seasonal weights to the base case.
strategy_specs.provenance: Weights and the 200-day window chosen before the first run by a researcher who knew the presidential-cycle literature (Hirsch 1967) and its sample; no variants tried. Rule and parameters written before the first backtest run (4 Nov 2026), by a researcher who knew the historical record.
strategy_specs.missing_data: Engine rules (see module docstring); strategy-specific: no late-starting inputs.

strategy_specs.name: Policy-regime sector momentum
strategy_specs.thesis: Policy shocks (tariffs, healthcare subsidies, defence budgets, AI/data-centre scrutiny, clean-energy credits) create persistent sector trends; ride the strongest risk-adjusted trends, park unused slots in Treasuries.
